items.t: Columbia Valley is in Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area H, not in the City of Chilliwack, and Electoral Area H consists of Cultus Lake and Columbia Valley.
Electoral Area H borders Electoral Area E to the west, the City of Chilliwack to the north, the City of Abbotsford to the west, and the United States border to the south.
Columbia Valley sits south of Cultus Lake along Columbia Valley Highway, reaching toward the United States border, and is distinct from Cultus Lake Park itself.
The FVRD's Electoral Area H director page groups the area as Columbia Valley, Cultus Lake and Lindell Beach together under one director.
Columbia Valley Road is the road the FVRD evacuation guide names as serving much of the populated area around Cultus Lake.

Columbia Valley housing sits inside an electoral-area planning system, not a city zoning system: the FVRD's planning page lists the Official Community Plan (OCP) for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115, covering Columbia Valley, Lindell Beach and the Chilliwack River Valley, and the consolidated Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 for the electoral areas.

The FVRD states that Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 consolidates the nine existing zoning regulations for all of its electoral areas into one region-wide electoral area zoning bylaw, standardising regulations without significantly altering the regulations for a particular parcel or zone type.
A buyer should read the specific lot's zone under Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 rather than assume a city-style residential zone applies.

blocks.text: Columbia Valley: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The plan for this area is the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115, 2011, as amended, which guides land-use planning and management for Cultus Lake and Columbia Valley in Electoral Area H.
A buyer should confirm the lot's ALR status on the Agricultural Land Commission map and its zone under Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 before assuming a second dwelling or subdivision is permitted.

blocks.text: Columbia Valley: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Columbia Valley Community Hall at 1202 Kosikar Road is the named community hall for this valley, used for Columbia Valley ratepayers' meetings in the FVRD director's Area H updates.

The Columbia Valley Volunteer Fire Department is the named emergency response organisation for the valley in the FVRD's Area H evacuation guide, alongside the Cultus Lake Volunteer Fire Department, BC Ambulance, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and Search and Rescue.

Electoral Area H spans nearly 110 square kilometres and includes Columbia Valley, Cultus Lake and Lindell Beach, with a permanent population of over 2,500 people largely located in and around Cultus Lake, per the FVRD evacuation guide.

Parking on Columbia Valley Highway is prohibited because it presents a hazard to drivers and pedestrians and prevents emergency services from moving safely, per the FVRD's Cultus Lake parking notice, so a buyer should not assume highway-shoulder parking is available at a lake-side home.

The Cultus Lake Park office, at 4165 Columbia Valley Highway, is the administration office for Cultus Lake Park, a separate jurisdiction from the Columbia Valley electoral-area lots south of the park.

The FVRD's 2026 Area H residential utility sheet lists only Cultus Lake service areas: Water – Cultus Lake is listed as no utility billing, Sewer – Cultus Lake North is a flat rate of $1,369.00, and Sewer – Cultus Lake South is listed as no utility billing, with utility bills issued annually in January in arrears through utility billing user fees in addition to taxation.

No Columbia Valley water or sewer service area is listed on that 2026 Area H sheet, so a Columbia Valley buyer should confirm whether the specific lot is on a private well and septic system and budget for that servicing rather than assume an FVRD utility connection.
Garbage is a private cost here because the FVRD does not provide garbage and recycling services in Electoral Area H, as stated on its facilities page.

Columbia Valley Highway is the corridor out of the valley north toward Cultus Lake and Chilliwack, and it is the highway named in the FVRD's Cultus Lake parking notice as the route where parking is prohibited.

The FVRD evacuation guide states Columbia Valley Road provides one-way in and one-way out access for much of the populated area around Cultus Lake, and notes limited alternative emergency egress routes were explored in a 2012 traffic study.

Seasonal bus service reaches Cultus Lake only in the BC Transit guide: Route 56 Cultus Lake is listed for the July 1 to Labour Day period, and no fixed route into Columbia Valley itself is stated in that guide.

blocks.text: Columbia Valley: risks and due diligence

items.t: Read the FVRD Electoral Area H evacuation guide for the specific property before removing subjects: the guide covers evacuation assumptions, narrow road corridors, traffic congestion, and the single-access character of the Columbia Valley Road area.

Confirm water and sewer servicing lot by lot: the 2026 Area H utility sheet lists only Cultus Lake service areas, so a Columbia Valley lot may depend on a private well and septic system whose condition and capacity need their own checks.

Check wildfire interface and FireSmart readiness: the FVRD director's Area H updates record FireSmart demonstrations for the area, including a demonstration site at Twin Alders across from the Cultus Lake Community Hall, and the FVRD's preparedness materials list Columbia Valley among its electoral-area communities.
Check ALR status and zone under Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 on the Agricultural Land Commission map and the FVRD planning page, because rural lots here can carry both ALR and rural-zone constraints.

blocks.text: What is not confirmed about Columbia Valley

items.t: Whether a specific Columbia Valley lot is inside the ALR; the zone, minimum lot size and second-dwelling rules for any specific Columbia Valley lot under Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 (to be read lot by lot); whether any Columbia Valley lot is served by an FVRD water or sewer service area (the 2026 Area H sheet lists only Cultus Lake service areas); whether a specific Columbia Valley lot falls in a designated speculation and vacancy tax taxable area; any current Columbia Valley subdivision or development application, including whether the FVRD's 43940 Frost Road Area H application sits in Columbia Valley or in Cultus Lake South; a Columbia Valley-wide housing-stock profile; a fixed BC Transit route into Columbia Valley itself; measured drive times to Chilliwack or the border; school catchment for a specific Columbia Valley address.

faq.a: No, it is in the Fraser Valley Regional District. The FVRD's Official Community Plan amendment record states that Electoral Area H consists of Cultus Lake and Columbia Valley, and the FVRD director page groups Columbia Valley with Cultus Lake and Lindell Beach under Electoral Area H. That means services, bylaws and tax bills come from the regional district and the Province, not from Chilliwack City Hall.
faq.q: Is Columbia Valley in the City of Chilliwack?

faq.a: The FVRD does not provide it here. The FVRD facilities page states the FVRD does not provide garbage and recycling services in Electoral Areas D, E or H, and that residents may arrange pickup through a private waste hauler or take garbage to the Bailey Landfill in Chilliwack. A buyer should therefore confirm private hauler availability for the specific road before assuming curbside collection.
faq.q: Who picks up garbage in Columbia Valley?

faq.a: In practical terms, yes for the lake-side populated area. The FVRD's Electoral Area H evacuation guide states that Columbia Valley Road, serving much of the populated area around Cultus Lake, provides one-way in and one-way out access only, and that communities on the southern end of Cultus Lake may be unable to use Columbia Valley Highway in an emergency. A buyer should read the evacuation guide for the specific property.
faq.q: Is there one road in and out?

faq.a: The guide's seasonal Route 56 Cultus Lake serves Cultus Lake in the July 1 to Labour Day period, which is the lake end of the corridor, not the Columbia Valley side south of the lake, so a buyer should plan on driving and confirm any seasonal service at the time of purchase.
